relevance_note: Single case report of a 16-year-old female given a clinical (imaging-based) diagnosis: "a diagnosis of coarctation of the aorta with arterial tortuosity syndrome was made"; no SLC2A10 testing or variant is reported, so the person is in scope by diagnosis only.
method_note: Read by hand; no script transcribed any table (the paper has none). One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No genetic testing or SLC2A10 variant is mentioned anywhere, so the variants table is empty. n_patients_reported (patients with a SLC2A10 variant) left null because the paper states no such patient. No age at diagnosis is stated; the 16-year age is the age at presentation, recorded as age at last evaluation. Vital status not stated. Country not stated (only the institution 'Spectra Health Imaging and Interventional Radiology'). 'There were no clear dysmorphic features' was recorded as an excluded feature but not used to exclude 'down-slanting palpebral fissures' (hedged and broader). 'The aorta was normal in caliber from the origin to the bifurcation' (abdominal angiogram) is recorded as written; it is not used for the checklist because the thoracic CT showed narrowing. Tortuosity is reported only for the descending aorta; the dilated/anomalous abdominal and chest wall arteries are not described as tortuous, so 'tortuosity of arteries other than the aorta' is not reported. Figure 2 legend calls it 'sclerosing tortuosity involving the proximal part of the descending thoracic aorta'. The Discussion says patient was 'treated with Nifedipine ... before she was referred', consistent with the Clinical Presentation. No internal contradictions found.
